Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
- Objective: scope POC decision criteria for deployment mode: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Agree success criteria (latency, cost, quality), workload sizing, benchmark plan, and timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, um i'm sofia from redwood, i'll let marcus say hi and then we can jump into goals for this call 
[00:06] Marcus: hey all, marcus liang here, i'm the solutions eng, focusing on performance and deploy. quick agenda, lena - we want to understand your traffic patterns, success criteria, and decide whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense for the POC.
[00:20] Lena: hi, lena here. thanks. our main driver is to reduce latency for our inference endpoints for multi-turn chat and summarization across internal docs. we also have strict data retention rules for some customers, so that is on the checklist.
[00:33] Tom: tom, devops. i'll own infra stuff for the POC. happy to share our k8s config and network constraints.
[00:38] Priya: priya - we own model infra and evals. current stack is hosted on our cloud, using a mix of g4 and g5 for training; inferencing today is a mix of self-hosted and upstream APIs (we use openai for some tasks).
[00:50] Sofia: quick qualification Qs: what are your p95 latency targets? what throughput do we expect? and do you have an internal cost-per-query target?
[01:02] Lena: p95 ideally under 250ms for short queries (<256 tokens), and under 600ms for longer flows (~512-1024 tokens). throughput during peak is about 250 concurrent users, each doing ~1 req / 10s, so roughly 25 req/s sustained but with spikes to 120 req/s. cost target is rough, we want to be comparable to openai at current spend but less variability.
[01:28] Marcus: ok that maps to like 25-120 rps. for sizing we'll need average token length - do you have tokens per request?
[01:36] Priya: avg is 180 tokens out, 120 in, so ~300 tokens total per request. sometimes there are long summarization jobs up to 3k tokens but those are <1% of calls.
[01:48] Marcus: perfect. so rough baseline - hosted can get you started quickly for functional validation and quality checks. Dedicated is good when you want predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Private if you need VPC-only or on-prem air-gap, or strict e-privacy regs.
[02:05] Lena: we have some customers in EU with data residency demands, but for the POC we can scope with EU workloads anonymized. Not sure yet if full Private is needed.
[02:14] Tom: also curious about SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration - these are must-haves for any enterprise test.
[02:21] Sofia: yep we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated; Hosted has managed KMS and SOC2 cert. we'll share security pack.
[02:33] Priya: how about model variants - can you route to a quantized variant to save cost? and what about continuous batching impacting tail latency?
[02:43] Marcus: good Q. we support model variants and quantized artifacts; smart routing can send non-critical traffic to quantized models. batching is continuous and adaptive - it reduces cost but we can enforce latency SLOs with a max-batch-delay override. you'll see tradeoffs: batching yields better cost-per-token but increases p95 if bursty with small qps.
[03:05] Lena: can we run a benchmark that simulates our exact request mix? preferrably with warm KV cache to account for prefix caching?
[03:13] Marcus: yes - we like to do two-phase benchmark: (1) cold-start single-shot latency across sequence lengths; (2) steady-state throughput with your request mix and warm-KV/ prefix cache. we'll need a 1-week sample of production traffic or synthetic workload to mimic.
[03:28] Tom: network egress - if we do Dedicated in a customer VPC, how does routing work? do we tunnel traffic back to your control plane?
[03:36] Marcus: Dedicated in customer VPC can be set up with private peering, and control plane traffic is minimal. For Private on-prem, control plane can be customer-managed and API traffic stays in your network. We'll share a diagram. sometimes the transcript generator garbles it as "control plane peering" -> "control plain pairing" in notes, so watch for that.
[03:50] Sofia: ok let's talk success criteria - what would you consider a 'pass' for the POC?
[03:55] Lena: three things: 1) latency p95 under 300ms for our main chat flow (<512 tokens) in steady-state; 2) quality parity within 5% of our current best model (we'll measure with eval set); 3) unit cost improvement or predictable cost with SLA compared to current managed endpoints.
[04:12] Priya: and operational - ability to access logs, SSO, and 30d retention of traces for debugging.
[04:19] Marcus: noted. we'll define a scoring rubric: latency (40%), quality (40%), ops (+security) (20%). We'll produce a benchmark report with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost-per-token estimates for different quantization levels.
[04:33] Lena: timeline? we have a board review 5 weeks out and want recommended direction by then.
[04:40] Sofia: propose 4-week POC: week 1 - baseline hosted runs (sanity + eval), week 2 - run Dedicated sizing + config, week 3 - Dedicated pilot benchmark, week 4 - analysis + decision and board deck. If Private required, that adds planning and legal (NDA + security review) and likely 6-8 weeks.
[04:58] Tom: for Dedicated sizing you mentioned GPU types and concurrency. what do you recommend for 25-120 rps with ~300 tokens avg?
[05:06] Marcus: rough math: with Redwood runtime on A100/ H100-like performance, but we need to assume quantization and concurrency - for 120 rps peak with p95 targets, you'd want about 2-4 GPUs of high-memory cards with autoscaling headroom, or a pool of several smaller GPUs with GPU multiplexing. We'll send a sizing worksheet with throughput per GPU estimates (we'll include latency curves).
[05:26] Priya: can we do cost modeling? i.e., compare hosted e2e cost vs Dedicated monthly commit?
[05:31] Sofia: yes, our pricing sheet includes usage-based hosted tokens and Dedicated commit examples; tradeoffs are that Dedicated reduces unit-cost at commit but needs heavier ops for scaling/maintenance, though Redwood handles most runtime ops. We'll include an example using your traffic numbers.
[05:45] Lena: security concerns - we need SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and penetration test reports. Also, EU data residency for some customer segments.
[05:55] Sofia: we have SOC2 and ISO; Private deployment is best for strict residency and air-gap needs. For Dedicated we can provision in EU region and support customer-managed KMS for encryption in-transit and at-rest. we'll attach certs.
[06:10] Tom: any limitations around third-party model licensing? we use some foundation models with restrictive licenses.
[06:17] Marcus: licensing varies by model. Redwood catalogs model profiles and notes licensing. For POC just pick an OS model or a licensed partner model; we'll confirm license compatibility. Also note some transcription errors will show model names like "gpt-three" vs "gpt-4" incorrectly in auto notes.
[06:33] Priya: for benchmarks, can you give us the terraform snippets or helm charts to spin up the dedicated agents? we'd prefer terraform.
[06:40] Marcus: yes - we have a dedicated terraform module and an example helm chart for private. Marcus: I'll send a minimal terraform snippet as part of the benchmark pack.
[06:49] Sofia: ok let's capture explicit acceptance criteria and timeline to include in the POC doc.
[06:53] Lena: acceptance: p95 <300ms, quality delta <=5% on eval set, cost per 1M tokens <= $X (we'll define X after you send pricing). Also operational: SSO, KMS, audit logs present.
[07:08] Sofia: i'll log that in the POC doc. We'll also run an A/B between hosted and dedicated in week 3 to show delta.
[07:15] Tom: for the A/B, will warm KV cache be comparable? how do you ensure fairness?
[07:20] Marcus: we'll run long enough to warm caches and then run steady-state traffic for both. we'll also provide raw logs and measurement methodology.
[07:31] Priya: small nit - what's the expected ticket to production if we choose Dedicated after POC? how long for rollout?
[07:38] Sofia: if you sign a reserved capacity contract, Dedicated rollout to production typically 2-6 weeks depending on network setup and region; Private on-prem instead can be 6-12 weeks including security and legal.
[07:50] Lena: ok great. any blockers from our side? we need to confirm legal for data sharing and provide anonymized traffic by next Tuesday.
[07:58] Tom: i'll coordinate with security and legal.
[08:01] Sofia: recap of next steps: 1) Sofia send sizing worksheet + pricing (due 4/12). 2) Marcus send benchmark plan + terraform snippet (due 4/13). 3) Cascade shares anonymized traffic and eval prompts (due 4/14). 4) schedule benchmark week of 4/20.
[08:18] Lena: sounds good. thanks all.
[08:21] Sofia: thanks everyone. we'll attach security docs and a draft POC SOW in the follow up email.

End of meeting
